description: Member of Technical Staff, Clinical Data & Statistical Programming Our mission is to advance humanity's ability to engineer biology. We approach this by understanding and improving AI’s application to biology across basic research, drug discovery, and biosecurity. We are a team of engineers, scientists, and operations specialists who are driven by improving capabilities and interpretability. Some of our work is showcased on benchmarks.bio . About this role. You will build evaluations of the work that turns clinical protocols and study records into trustworthy datasets and reproducible results. The role has two tracks: Clinical data management: Designing data collection, configuring study databases, and managing queries, reconciliation, and data quality. Statistical programming: Writing and validating code in SAS, R, or Python to construct analysis datasets, implement prespecified analyses, and produce clinical-trial tables, listings, and figures. We welcome candidates with depth in either track. Your initial roadmap will draw on that expertise, with the broader function growing through collaboration and hiring. This is a high-intensity, founder-type role. Our Members of Technical Staff have built companies, run drug programs and scaled complex technical projects. What you will do: - Build evaluations around data-capture requirements, database logic, edit checks, queries, and reconciliation across study sources. - Develop tasks that test agents writing and validating code for analysis-dataset construction, derivations, traceability, and production of clinical-trial tables, listings, and figures. - Create reference outputs and checks that identify consequential errors in data processing and programmed analyses. - Work with engineers to run agents and investigate whether outputs are correct, reproducible, and consistent with study requirements. - Build the first evaluations yourself, then recruit and lead experts across the function's complementary specialties. What we look for: - Substantial experience delivering clinical databases, study datasets, or programmed analyses for real studies. - Depth in at least one track: clinical data management or statistical programming. Statistical programming candidates should have strong hands-on coding ability in SAS, R, or Python, including validation and reproducibility. - Scientific curiosity, comfort learning AI tools, and the judgment and initiative to build a team responsible for high-quality output. We welcome scientists who have become fluent with AI tools and quantitative or engineering researchers with substantial hands-on experience in the relevant domain. How we work. description: Member of Technical Staff, Experimental Biology & Assay Development Our mission is to advance humanity's ability to engineer biology. We approach this by understanding and improving AI’s application to biology across basic research, drug discovery, and biosecurity. We are a team of engineers, scientists, and operations specialists who are driven by improving capabilities and interpretability. Some of our work is showcased on benchmarks.bio . About this role. You will translate practical experimental expertise into evaluations of AI systems that plan, troubleshoot, and interpret laboratory work. You will define the research roadmap, build the first evaluations, and recruit a team. You will also help shape experiments performed with our research and CRO partners. This is a high-intensity, founder-type role. Our Members of Technical Staff have built companies, run drug programs and scaled complex technical projects. What you will do: - Develop evaluations around assay selection, controls, experimental conditions, troubleshooting, and interpretation of ambiguous results. - Work with partner laboratories to define experiments, review execution, and capture raw data, metadata, deviations, and negative results. - Build tasks that test whether an agent can choose an informative next experiment and recognize unreliable evidence. - Collaborate with engineers to run agents, examine their failures, and develop grading methods grounded in experimental reality. - Recruit, train, and lead scientists while maintaining responsibility for scientific quality and delivery. title: Cell Culture Engineer
description: Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world. We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today. Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development. We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation. About the Role We're expanding our protein expression into mammalian cell culture, for example in CHO and HEK cells. Our mammalian expression volume is growing fast. We're looking for a Cell Culture Engineer who has spent years growing and transfecting mammalian cells and knows what to do when a run goes wrong. You'll work alongside our production and mammalian cell teams as a hands-on expert in the cell culture lab. You'll keep cultures healthy and on schedule, run transfections and expressions, and be the person the team turns to when yields drop or cells misbehave. This is a hands-on role, not a management role. What You'll Do Run mammalian expression. Maintain, expand, and passage cell lines, and run transfections and expressions on a production schedule. Troubleshoot. When viability, growth, or yield falls off, find the cause and fix it. Own the cell bank. Thaw, freeze, and track cell stocks, and protect the lines from contamination and drift. Optimize conditions. Test culture and transfection conditions, and turn what works into the standard protocol. Scale with automation. Work with our automation team to move cell handling onto liquid handlers as volume grows. Hand off clean material. Deliver harvests ready for purification and downstream assays. Keep the lab running. Look after incubators, biosafety cabinets, and cell counters, and keep the BSL-2 space organized and compliant. Write SOPs and train. Document protocols that others can follow, and train the team on aseptic technique and our cell culture workflows. What We're Looking For Extensive hands-on experience with common mammalian model cell lines, for example CHO and HEK, including transfection and expression. BSc / MSc in biotechnology, cell biology, or a relevant field. A troubleshooting track record. You've rescued failing cultures and expressions and can explain what went wrong and why. Flawless aseptic technique and experience working under BSL-2 conditions. Experience with high-throughput formats: multi-well plates and many conditions in parallel, not only flasks. Experience with liquid handlers is a plus. Experience with antibody or Fc-fusion production is a plus. Organized and precise. You track every stock, passage, and transfection, and you follow protocols exactly. You use AI tools effectively and with discernment. We use them across the company and expect you to check, edit, and stand behind what they produce, not pass along unreviewed output. Comfortable in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift. Cells don't keep office hours, so you plan around them. Application deadline We are reviewing applicants on a rolling basis. Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Project Manager, Medical Affairs
description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a Project Manager to join our growing Medical Affairs team!  

The Project Manager is responsible for delivering assigned medical affairs projects from initiation through final closeout, including planning, coordination, budget management, routing, approvals, and launch of project deliverables. Projects may include slide decks, print projects, congress materials, advisory board materials, scientific communications, and smaller digital initiatives. This role serves as a main point of contact across internal and external teams, partnering closely with Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, User Experience, Technology, and Quality Assurance partners to keep work on time, on budget, and aligned to client expectations.

Whether it’s bringing in the right resources at the right time, aligning priorities with the account team, or identifying bottlenecks and proposing solutions early, no two days are the same.  

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago or Indianapolis—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs. This role will primarily work Eastern business hours.

What you’ll do:  

  • Clearly communicate expectations to internal teams and vendors to support the efficient flow of work throughout the agency.
  • Partner with key agency teams to ensure projects stay on track and agreed-upon milestones are met, including Account, Scientific/Medical, Editorial, Creative, Studio, Print Production, Strategic Planning, Information UX, Technology, and Programming teams.
  • Plan, schedule, and monitor work to meet timeline, budget, and quality goals in accordance with relevant guidelines. 
  • Collaborate with finance and accounting teams on revenue recognition/invoicing processes 
  • Participate in client and stakeholder meetings as needed, with a clear understanding of project status and timelines to respond to relevant questions and provide project updates when appropriate.
  • Perform risk planning and mitigation to minimize project risk. 
  • Help create service or departmental standard operating procedures 
  • Route deliverables to appropriate core team members for review and signoff via the electronic project routing system.  
  • Ensure signoff prior to key milestones, including core team review, medical/scientific review, client review, vendor handoff, and final release.
  • Develop detailed work plans, schedules, and status reports to keep internal teams, clients, and external partners aligned throughout the project life cycle. 
  • Serve as a day-to-day project lead, helping define scope and objectives while motivating cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality work on time and on budget. 
  • Coordinate project deliverables from concept through delivery, ensuring the appropriate internal departments, reviews, approvals, and handoffs are engaged at each stage. 
  • Support adherence to agency process and manage the quality assurance phase for all projects.

This position is a perfect fit for you if:  

  • Our Company values – Best Together, Impact-Obsessed, Excellence Expected, Evolve Always and Accountability with an “I” – really speak to you.
  • You are adaptable, resilient, and OK with adjusting your scope, responsibilities, and focus as we grow. When things change, so do we. We’re always evolving.
  • You are proactive, driven, and resourceful with strong prioritization skills and a desire to dive into the data.
  • You are a highly organized self-starter who can work independently and manage tight deadlines.

What you should have:  

  • 3+ years of Project/Program Management or relevant experience. 
  • 2+ years of experience in budget management. 
  • Working familiarity with industry-specific processes, including medical, legal, regulatory, and client review.
  • Background working on teams focused on medical affairs, scientific communications, medical education, or related non-promotional healthcare communications projects.
  • Demonstrated track record of leading small- to medium-scale projects from conception through completion. 
  • Experience working cross-functionally with medical/scientific, editorial, account, creative, and project management partners to deliver high-quality products and services. 
  • Proficient in creating timelines and tracking progress against schedules.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with technical and non-technical teams across multiple business areas; excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

title: Associate Medical Writer - allegro.WRITE at Inizio Medical
description:
Associate Medical Writer

Inizio Medical – allegro.WRITE

Locations: Manchester, Macclesfield, Glasgow, London

Start Date: Feb 2027

 

Medical communications: entry-level training programme – allegro.WRITE

What is allegro.WRITE?

Are you a first-class communicator who is passionate about improving the lives of patients through scientific communications? Do you want a challenging, yet rewarding career at the forefront of the healthcare industry working on cutting-edge science? If so, medical writing might be the career for you ….

We’re looking for high calibre, enthusiastic and motivated aspiring writers to join Inizio Medical through our multi-award-winning training and development programme, allegro.WRITE.

 

allegro.WRITE is a comprehensive, year-long programme, designed to equip you for a role as a Medical Writer with Inizio Medical – a company including three of the world-leading medical communications agencies: ApotheCom, Ashfield MedComms and Nucleus Global. Successful candidates join our business as an Associate Medical Writer, on a full-time contract. The programme comprises an initial, dedicated training phase, followed by a team placement within the business to gain varied, real-life med comms experience. You will join energetic and passionate teams, building your confidence and ability by working alongside some of the most talented people in the industry. After 12 months, you will leave allegro.WRITE as a fully-fledged Medical Writer and become an integral part of an account team at one of our agencies, delivering contemporary, multichannel medical communications solutions to our clients!

What do I need?

To be considered for the role you must have a minimum of a 2:1 in a Life Sciences degree. No previous writing experience is necessary, but good written and verbal communication skills, an awareness of the pharmaceutical industry, a keen eye for detail, and a passion for knowledge are important! You must have a full right to work in the UK and be available for training across July and August.

What’s the recruitment process?

To apply, please send us your CV, together with a biography of ≤500 words, highlighting your skills, interests and relevant experience. Please combine your CV and biography in one document.

Suitable candidates will be asked to take a formal writing test, followed by the final stages of the process, which will be scheduled for December. The job commences in February 2027 and will run from our Manchester, Macclesfield, London and Glasgow offices.

What are the benefits of joining Inizio Medical?

As one of our writers, you’ll benefit from a defined career path, diverse project work, competitive salary and benefits, and opportunities to travel the world!

As part of allegro.WRITE, you will have tailored and dedicated training, coaching and mentoring, alongside ‘on the job’ experience with nurturing teams. As you progress in your career, you will also have the option to join our allegro.EXCEL programme, supporting you in your development to senior scientific leadership roles at Inizio Medical!

Don't meet every job requirement? That's okay! Our company is dedicated to building an inclusive and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role, but your experience doesn't perfectly fit every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this role or others.

title: AI Solutions Program Manager, Finance
description:
Who we are  

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

You'll be joining the Finance Operational Excellence team, reporting to the Head of Finance Operational Excellence. We are finance transformation and AI experts working side-by-side with Finance, Product, and Engineering teams to redefine processes and build the finance organization of the future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys working across disciplines: part solution developer, part data architect, part workflow designer, and part coach. You’ll have room to shape how applied AI is built and scaled both from a technical and end-user perspective.

What you’ll do

You'll work side-by-side with Finance subject matter experts to understand how work gets done, identify the highest impact opportunities, and partner with domain teams to chart a transformation plan which balances future ambitions with rapid impact.  You'll work independently to automate manual processes, design and build agents and required data solutions using internal platforms, and enable Finance teams to maintain these solutions long-term. 

You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next. 

You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.

This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.

Responsibilities

  • Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.
  • Build and operationalize AI agents for Finance use cases, delivering end-to-end solutions from prototype through validation, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.
  • Write and optimize SQL for data extraction, transformation, calculation, and validation, ensuring Finance-facing outputs are accurate, explainable, and reliable.
  • Design reusable knowledge layers, evaluation methods, validation patterns, data-quality frameworks, and components that improve agent accuracy and accelerate future use cases.
  • Identify agentic limitations and new possibilities; determine when to use existing capabilities, develop an alternative approach, or partner with Engineering to scope and test custom tools and integrations, including tools using Model Context Protocol where appropriate.
  • Build alongside users, gather feedback through real deliverables, and iterate until the solution fits the workflow and earns user trust.
  • Enable long-term ownership through clear SOPs, runbooks, training, and self-service tooling; coach Finance teams to operate, maintain, and evolve what has been built.
  • Establish monitoring and observability for deployed agents, including metrics, alerting, and incident-response processes that support reliable operation.
  • Diagnose technical and data issues, resolve problems independently where possible, and collaborate with Engineering when solutions require deeper platform changes.
  • Measure adoption and impact, share lessons and wins, and turn successful implementations into standards, components, and playbooks for the broader Finance AI portfolio.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in data analytics, technical operations, business intelligence, automation, solutions delivery, or a related field.
  • Of which, 2+ years of experience in program management, working directly alongside business leaders to develop and execute process transformation programs
  • Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools, agents, automations, or workflows that changed a real business process—not solely using AI as a conversational tool, 
  • Strong SQL proficiency, including experience writing complex queries using CTEs, window functions, and joins for data analysis, transformation, or pipeline logic.
  • A track record of independently scoping and delivering technical solutions for process improvement, demonstrating ownership from problem definition through adoption.
  • Strong analytical and investigative skills, including the ability to identify root causes, debug complex data problems, and resolve inconsistencies.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and work effectively with domain experts and Engineering partners.
  • Experience teaching, coaching, enabling users, or transferring ownership of a solution through documentation, training, or self-service tools.
  • Working knowledge of development practices such as version control, testing, code review, and iterative delivery.
  • Experience using low-code tools, scripting, workflow automation, AI-assisted development, or custom integrations, paired with curiosity and the ability to learn evolving technologies.

You will also likely have (not required):

  • Domain experience in Finance Operations, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Payments, or other areas.
  • Familiarity with modern data tools and practices, such as Python, Databricks, ETL/ELT processes, data pipelines, and data-quality controls.
  • Experience with Model Context Protocol or another extensibility or integration framework.
  • Experience navigating financial systems and understanding how data flows through accounting, reporting, reconciliation, forecasting, or payments processes.
  • Experience with change management, organizational transformation, or large-scale enablement programs.
  • Experience building internal tools, templates, components, or playbooks that were adopted beyond the original team or use case.
  • Experience working in a high-growth technology company with rapidly evolving processes and tools.

Note on technical depth: This role involves working at the intersection of no-code AI tools and custom development. While software engineering expertise is not required, you should be comfortable applying technical concepts, collaborating closely with Engineering teams, and using AI-assisted development tools to extend platform capabilities when needed.

title: Clinical Data Operator - Austin, TX
description:
POSITION SUMMARY:  On site position in Austin, TX

Clinical Data Operator accessions patient samples according to standard operating procedures (SOP) with high efficiency and accuracy.  Hourly rate starts at $18.
 
Shift Options:
Tuesday - Saturday,  7am-330pm 
Hourly rate starts at $18
     
 
PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

*Front-end lab operations*
- Receive, sort, and transport packages from the shipping dock and reception to the Accessioning lab, and scan tracking numbers accurately.
- Open, prep, and de-kit samples, checking that paperwork matches samples and that no PHI or samples remain in discarded kit boxes.
- Rack bulk samples and distribute work to stations according to distribution guidelines.
- Support sample pickup, consolidation, and send-outs.
- Scan requisitions, bench worksheets, and supporting documents, and upload them to the correct case.
- File, store, and dispose of requisition forms according to retention requirements.
- Empty bins, carts, trash, and biohazard containers, and keep workstations and lab areas clean and organized.

*Case creation and data entry*
- Capture requisition and case information using intelligent document processing (IDP) tools such as Fusion.
- As trained: create new orders in the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), enter and review patient data, and keep records accurate and up to date.
- As trained: accession samples across product types with high accuracy and efficiency.

*Quality, safety, and compliance*
- Handle samples (blood, buccal, and tissue) and package-opening tools safely and correctly.
- Escalate packaging issues, discrepancies, or quality concerns to Leads or Supervisors.
- Follow SOPs, quality standards, and safety requirements, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
- This role works with PHI regularly in both paper and electronic form, and has access to various technologies to access PHI in order to do the job. Protect PHI at all times in line with HIPAA and privacy policies.
- Complete HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance, and security training as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after hire.
- Maintain current status on all Natera training requirements.
- Perform other duties as assigned.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT**
- Stand and walk for most of the shift, up to 8–10 hours.
- Lift, carry, push, and pull up to 50 lbs regularly, including boxes, totes, and loaded carts.
- Bend, reach, stoop, and kneel repeatedly.
- Perform repetitive hand and wrist motions, including scanning, opening packages, and typing.
- Work in a clinical lab environment with possible exposure to biological samples and biohazardous materials, using required PPE.
- Work in a fast-paced, high-volume, deadline-driven environment.
- Be flexible for shift changes, weekends, holidays, and overtime based on business needs.

**QUALIFICATIONS**
- High school diploma (or equivalent) required.
- 0–1 year of experience in a lab, warehouse, logistics, healthcare, or data entry setting preferred.
- Previous computer experience required.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in high-volume, physical work.
- Willingness to do hands-on tasks of every kind as part of a team.
- Ability to learn several workflows and systems, and build toward full accessioning.
- Typing speed of at least 45 wpm with high accuracy, or the ability to reach it during training.
- Good oral and written communication skills, and sound judgment.
- Reliable, organized, self-motivated, and able to work well with others.

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management.

WHAT WE OFFER

title: Alliance Partner Manager (SaaS) | Luma
description:
Our Why At Dotmatics 

At Dotmatics, a Siemens company,  we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.

We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.

We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.

Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.

Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics 

Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.

You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation.  Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.

We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together. 

What do we need

We are seeking an Alliance Partner Manager to lead the technical dimension of our alliances and partnering function for Luma, our AI-Native Multimodal Research Platform for Scientific Intelligence. Sitting at the intersection of business and engineering, you'll own how our platform connects with, integrates into, and creates value alongside the products of our strategic technology partners, such as Databricks and AWS.

This position is based in EMEA, working globally across time zones. It is a senior role with broad scope, where you'll act as the bridge between partner engineering teams and our own product, engineering and commercial organizations, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales, as well as colleagues at Siemens, with room to design and build the technical alliance capability around you.

While the focus is strategic, this remains a hands-on role: you'll need enough technical depth to scope integrations credibly, validate them in sandboxes, and hold your own in a conversation with a partner's engineering team. We're looking for someone with an engineering-minded, "application scientist" type approach — comfortable understanding the technical requirements involved in onboarding a partner, and operating confidently within a large company mindset and environment.

In this role you will get to:

  • Define, build, and execute the technical partner strategy, prioritising which integrations and joint solutions to build, developing and implementing joint go-to-market plans (co-sell, co-build, co-deliver), aligning teams and facilitating sales enablement and training of partners.
  • Own engineering level relationships across partner organisations through effective communication, structured governance and business reviews, and joint business planning.
  • Scope integration feasibility early in partner conversations, translating vague partner asks into clear, buildable technical specifications and setting realistic expectations.
  • Oversee solution architecture, use-case mapping, partner product certification and sandbox / proof-of-concept development to design and validate joint solutions.
  • Engage partners to develop differentiated solutions through joint collaboration, market and competitive analysis, and the creation of joint marketing collateral.
  • Evangelise partnerships internally, working closely with Sales, Legal, Marketing, Engineering, Product, Support and Pre-Sales stakeholders, and with colleagues at Siemens, feeding partner needs into the roadmap and organising collaborative events.
  • Define, track and analyse key partnership metrics, collaborating with partners to optimise performance, and represent Dotmatics/Siemens at alliance and partner conferences and events.
  • Focus specifically on systems integration partners, bringing on partners that will meaningfully increase the bottom line.

We are looking for candidate's who have 7+ years in technology partnerships, alliances, solution architecture or pre-sales engineering, including several years leading strategic technical partner or ISV relationships at enterprise scale. You've built integrations, not just managed them, and you can move fluently between a business review and a whiteboard session with a partner's engineers. You're comfortable operating with a high degree of autonomy on complex, ambiguous pursuits, and you set realistic expectations that engineering can actually deliver on.

Just as importantly, you lead through influence. You can align engineering, marketing and sales teams, internally and across partner organisations, behind a shared plan without direct authority, and you're motivated by building a partnering function and team, not just running one. While not a traditional "sales" person, you're comfortable navigating sales-style conversations, combining technical knowledge with strong relationship management and communication skills.

Given the scientific focus of the Luma platform, experience in scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology would be particularly valuable. We're interested in candidates who understand the challenges of scientific research, including scientific data, laboratory workflows and the technology platforms that support R&D.

Key Skills:

  • Technical partnership leadership - a proven track record defining and executing partner or alliance strategy with ISVs, technology platforms or system integrators, with measurable partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue impact.
  • Hands-on integration fluency, including practical depth with APIs, authentication and data-exchange patterns, and the ability to scope, spec and validate integrations through sandboxes and proof-of-concept builds.
  • Joint go-to-market execution - experience developing co-sell, co-build and co-deliver plans, aligning internal and partner teams, facilitating sales enablement and creating the collateral that makes joint solutions land.
  • Executive-level relationship management - comfort owning senior stakeholder relationships across partner organisations, running structured business reviews (QBRs), and resolving conflict constructively when internal and partner priorities clash.
  • Data-driven partner management, with the habit of defining, tracking and analysing partnership KPIs and leading indicators of partner health and acting on them before issues escalate.

You may also have:

  • Experience with cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) or OEM / embedded partnership motions.
  • Experience structuring and negotiating complex commercial and technical agreements alongside legal teams.
  • Familiarity with tiered partner certification programmes.
  • Experience or familiarity with scientific software, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology or research-focused technology, including scientific data platforms, laboratory systems or R&D workflows. Experience in another domain-deep industry, such as Oil & Gas or Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), would also be valuable.

Research shows us the confidence gap and imposter syndrome can get in the way of meeting outstanding candidates, so please don’t hesitate to apply — we’d love to hear from you.

By submitting your application, you agree that Dotmatics may collect your personal data for recruiting, global organization planning, and related purposes. Dotmatics Privacy Notice explains what personal information we may process, where we may process your personal information, our purposes for processing your personal information, and the rights you can exercise over Dotmatics use of your personal information. 

Dotmatics is an equal opportunity employer. We are a welcoming place for everyone, and we do our best to make sure all people feel supported and connected at work.

title: CDI - Manager Product Engineer - Paris
description:
Mission

Ce que vous construisez ne reste pas à l’état de démonstration : de vrais utilisateurs, au sein de grands groupes, s’en servent chaque jour. Applications et agents se conçoivent et s’exploitent en binôme avec l’AI Product Manager. Une équipe sinistres retrouve ainsi sur un seul écran les documents utiles et un brouillon de réponse ; ailleurs, un processus de commande ne demande plus aucune ressaisie manuelle.

Ce poste est fait pour vous si vous voulez que de vrais utilisateurs s’appuient sur ce que vous livrez.

Artefact accompagne les plus grandes entreprises du monde dans le déploiement de l’IA : 3 000 AI makers dans plus de 30 pays, plus de 1 000 clients. En France, le département Engineering réunit environ 300 personnes sous la responsabilité du CTO ; vous y rejoignez le chapter AI Applied Engineer, archétype Product Engineer.

 

Activités et responsabilités

À chaque projet, l’AI Product Manager pilote le produit avec le client : ce qui se construit en premier, et la vérification que les utilisateurs s’en servent, se décident à deux.

Autour de l’application, trois métiers se croisent : les AI Engineers pour le comportement du modèle, les Platform Engineers pour le déploiement, les Context & Analytics Engineers pour les données dont l’application a besoin. Les tests se font avec les utilisateurs finaux, le code se relit entre pairs et les nouvelles recrues sont accompagnées.

 

Vos responsabilités :

  • Construire des applications métier : front end, back end et API.

  • Intégrer des agents et des assistants dans un processus métier, avec des contrôles humains là où ils comptent.

  • Automatiser des processus de bout en bout.

  • Intégrer un modèle dans un outil que les équipes utilisent déjà.

  • Construire les connecteurs dont le cas d’usage a besoin, par exemple un serveur MCP pour un outil métier.

  • Concevoir l’expérience utilisateur de l’IA : quand une personne valide, comment afficher les sources et l’incertitude.

  • Définir avec l’AI Product Manager les évaluations propres au cas d’usage et les suivre en production.

  • Assumer ce que vous livrez après la mise en production : monitoring, incidents, adoption.

 

Profil recherché

Les indispensables :

  1. Vous avez construit des applications avec un front end, un back end et des API, même si votre expertise est plus marquée d’un côté.

  2. Du code testé, relu et documenté, en Python, TypeScript ou dans un langage similaire.

  3. Les coding agents font déjà partie de votre quotidien, et vous vérifiez ce qu’ils produisent.

  4. Des besoins d’utilisateurs transformés en une première version, puis améliorée à partir de leurs retours.

  5. Le monitoring, les incidents et l’adoption font, pour vous, partie du métier.

  6. Une aisance à expliquer vos choix techniques à des personnes non techniques.

Un plus, pas un prérequis :

  • Une expérience de construction d’agents ou d’assistants au-dessus d’un LLM : appel d’outils, orchestration.

  • Une expérience de conception de parcours avec validation humaine (human-in-the-loop) ou d’interfaces d’IA.

  • Une expérience d’intégration à des logiciels métier, comme un ERP ou un CRM.

  • Une expérience au contact des clients.

Pas besoin de cocher toutes les cases pour postuler : si vous avez l’essentiel des indispensables et l’envie d’apprendre le reste, parlons-en.

 

Pourquoi nous rejoindre ?

Entre le produit, l’interface et le modèle, le Product Engineer occupe le point où l’IA rencontre ses utilisateurs. Leurs réactions s’observent directement, et chaque version livrée tient compte de ce que les usages ont révélé.

Nous sommes des AI makers : l’IA se construit avec nos clients, pas seulement pour eux. Leurs enjeux deviennent les nôtres, et nos choix techniques s’expliquent dans le langage du métier. Les positions que nous prenons sont claires ; elles évoluent face aux faits, jamais sous la pression.

Notre domaine change tous les mois, et ce rythme nous convient : les nouvelles technologies et les nouveaux secteurs s’apprennent vite, et les habitudes qui ne servent plus s’abandonnent sans regret. Devant un problème difficile, le réflexe est de le découper en étapes vérifiables, avec un haut niveau d’exigence sur le code comme sur les livrables.

Quand il manque quelque chose, pour un client ou pour le chapter, nous le construisons. La progression passe par des retours constructifs, par le partage des connaissances, par la demande d’aide sans attendre et par la reconnaissance du travail des autres. Il y a beaucoup à apprendre, et beaucoup à construire.

Un counsellor accompagne vos premiers mois. L’onboarding technique ouvre le parcours, suivi d’un premier projet client ; si aucun n’est prêt, les starter kits internes prennent le relais.

Le reste s’apprend sur les projets : conception d’agents, évaluation par cas d’usage, expérience utilisateur de l’IA, avec l’appui des AI Engineers et de la communauté Product Engineer. À partir de 2027, l’archétype Product Engineer disposera de sa propre grille de compétences et de son propre parcours de formation, en plus du socle commun à tous les AI Applied Engineers (évaluation de l’IA, responsabilité en production).

Plus tard, un rôle transverse devient possible (Project Tech Lead, Pre-sales Engineer, Engineering Manager), tout comme le chapter AI Product Manager.

 

Processus de recrutement

With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries. The team: With over 8 million signers sold worldwide, Ledger Wallet is where Ledger users manage and grow their assets. Transactional Services (buy, sell, swap, trading and stablecoin products) is its main source of service revenue. Money Flows connects users' crypto to the fiat world in both directions: on/off-ramp , cash-to-stablecoin , Card , and the growing P2P and Payments use cases. Users buy crypto with fiat or sell it back to their bank, move cash into stablecoins, and spend crypto with a card, all through specialist partners. It is the entry and exit door of the Ledger Wallet economy and a key lever to diversify Transactional Services revenue. The role reports to the Senior Director, Transactional Services. What you’ll be doing: You own and grow Money Flows end to end - revenue, economics, partner ecosystem and the quality of every fiat journey in Ledger Wallet - with a General Manager mindset over a business run mostly through external partners and cross-functional teams. The ambition is to grow revenue 10x in two to three years, through a strategy and roadmap you define and turn into quantified milestones. Key responsibilities include: Business Line Ownership & Revenue Delivery: Being ultimately accountable for Money Flows revenue, volume and take rate across buy, sell, cash-to-stablecoin, Card, P2P and Payments. Building and defending the forecast, querying the data yourself, and separating market effects from the levers the team controls. Monetization & Pricing: Owning take rate by line, partner and payment method. Turning volume into direct or indirect revenue (zero-fee partners, cash-to-stablecoin flows), and keeping pricing/product competitive against exchanges, neobanks and other wallets. Partner Management & Business Development: Identifying, signing, managing and negotiating with the ramp, payment, stablecoin and card-issuing partner bench - on pricing, geographic and payment-method coverage, conversion, KYC friction and operational quality. Managing concentration risk, onboarding new providers to close gaps, and running a monthly review with each partner. Card Programme Ownership: Running the card programme: economics, activation and dormancy, issuer and processor performance, card-scheme negotiations (including geo expansion), and the go-to-market with Marketing. Ledger Wallet Experience: Working with the Product Line Manager to improve the Buy, Sell, Card and Pay journeys, and making sure every release ships with a coordinated go-to-market. Stablecoin & Payments Roadmap: Shaping how Ledger captures stablecoin and payment use cases - cash-to-stablecoin, Pay and peer-to-peer flows - together with Product, within local regulatory frameworks (MiCA,...) with Legal and Compliance, informed by close tracking of the ramp, stablecoin and card landscape. Operational Excellence & Observability: Partner SLAs, incident management and fast action to protect users, Ledger and revenue; conversion, failed-payment and KYC-drop monitoring; and closing measurement gaps so every line can be steered on data. Cross-Functional Delivery: Driving execution across Product, Technology, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Pricing, Marketing/CRM and other business lines - all of it outside your reporting lines - to ship improvements, drive growth and resolve issues. What we’re looking for: Ownership mindset: A demonstrated ability to own a business line or revenue stream end to end and make data-driven decisions. You are energized by being accountable for a P&L line and delivering the budget, including in a soft market. Exceptional quantitative skills: A strong track record of using data to drive decisions and manage execution. You enjoy digging into the numbers yourself and separating market effect from execution. Commercial & business development experience: Proven results negotiating and managing external partners on pricing, terms and performance. The Growth Marketing Specialist role is a hands-on, delivery-focused position that keeps our new business engine running day to day.  What we can offer You'll receive up to a 7% pension contribution, life insurance, income protection, and private medical insurance for peace of mind. Access free counselling through our employee assistance program, as well as personalized health support. Enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey, as well as on-demand support from our partner Peppy. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business. We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy notice before applying to Avalere Health.

title: EH&S Lead
description:
About Arc Institute

Arc Institute is an independent nonprofit research organization at the interface of artificial intelligence and biology, working to accelerate scientific progress and understand the root causes of complex diseases. Founded in 2021 and based in Palo Alto, Arc partners with Stanford University, UC Berkeley, and UC San Francisco.

Unlike academia, our scientists have long-term funding and industry-like resources. Unlike industry, they're free to pursue high-risk, long-term research without commercial pressures. Arc's Technology Centers and Core Investigator labs work side by side, integrating experimental and computational biology under one roof to tackle problems neither could solve alone.

Our two Institute Initiatives reflect this model in action:

  • Virtual Cell Initiative: Building a full-stack virtual cell model to identify disease mechanisms and nominate drug targets,  accelerating the path from biological insight to clinical trials.
  • Alzheimer's Disease Initiative: Mapping the genes, pathways, and environmental factors behind Alzheimer's disease to develop drug candidates that address root causes.

More than 300 Arconauts work together at our Palo Alto headquarters, backed by substantial long-term philanthropic funding.

About the position

As EH&S Lead, you will own the development, implementation, and the management of Arc’s Environmental, Health, and Safety programs and culture. You will design solutions that satisfy overlapping local, state, and federal requirements, and serve as Arc’s primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies.

Your remit covers chemical hygiene, biosafety, OSHA compliance, medical and hazardous waste, and Arc’s safety permits and sustainability programs. You will hire and manage a biosafety manager and direct the work of outside vendors and consultants.

About you

  • You are deeply committed to the health and safety of your colleagues, and you achieve it through partnership with the labs rather than around them.
  • You are genuinely curious about the science here and want to understand the research at a real level of depth.
  • You thrive in a diverse environment and enjoy working with scientists and students from many backgrounds.
  • You are energized by building programs and forging cross-functional partnerships that strengthen the community and the mission.

In this position you will

  • Provide safety leadership and EH&S subject matter expertise aligned with Arc’s operating principles.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain EH&S programs, procedures, and systems in compliance with federal, state, and local regulations, driving continuous improvement.
  • Develop Arc’s safety strategy and carry out safety policies and procedures in accordance with all applicable regulatory and organizational requirements.
  • Hire, manage, and develop a biosafety manager, setting clear priorities and standards for their work.
  • Advise Arc’s administrative team on safety and compliance for specific projects and operations.
  • Define Arc’s approach to  EH&S employee safety and onboarding training, with a focus on efficiency and engagement.
  • Own and evolve Arc’s compliance programs including, but not limited to, the Cal/OSHA bloodborne pathogens standard and biosafety program, chemical safety, radiation safety, and controlled substances.
  • Own Arc’s environmental compliance strategy, including the industrial wastewater discharge permit, hazardous waste requirements, and regulatory permitting.
  • Own risk assessment program and conduct regular risk assessments and safety audits to identify workplace hazards — chemical, physical, biological, industrial, and radiological among them — and remediate hazards or recommend improvements to reduce them.
  • Lead investigations of accidents, incidents, injuries, and complaints concerning potential hazards or unsafe conditions to determine root causes and preventive measures.
  • Conduct safety inspections and walkthroughs that deliver meaningful insight and surface continuous improvement opportunities across Arc’s labs.
  • Develop and manage EH&S management systems covering chemical inventories, SDS, near-miss reporting, permitting compliance, and incident investigations.
  • Oversee regulated medical and hazardous waste programs, including vendor contracting.
  • Act as primary point of contact for regulatory and certifying agencies and government authorities.
  • Own procurement and maintenance of safety equipment and supply inventory, ensuring onsite personnel are adequately protected from workplace hazards.
  • Respond to emergency situations involving hazardous materials.
  • Develop, own and maintain Arc’s EH&S wiki.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in industrial hygiene, biology, chemistry, environmental science, occupational safety and health, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Master’s degree preferred.
  • 8+ years of laboratory experience, including 5 years in EH&S, with a minimum of 2 years leading and developing EH&S programs.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with a track record of managing multiple projects accurately and on time.
  • Working knowledge of the scientific and technical aspects of applicable regulations — including Cal/OSHA, CalEPA, the Medical Waste Management Act, EPA, DEA, OSHA, NRC, and NFPA — and how they bear on laboratory operations.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to prioritize resources, influence group behavior, and build consensus around safety practice.
  • Able to work independently and as part of a dynamic team, with a positive attitude, a strong sense of urgency, and a bias toward action.
  • Interest in learning new techniques, keeping accurate records, and working within established policies.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing people, including hiring, coaching, and developing direct reports.
  • Demonstrated success leading change management in a research or lab environment.
  • Experience with Animal Research Occupational Health and Safety programs.
  • Experience supporting laboratory animal research involving biohazardous or hazardous materials.
  • Associate Safety Professional (ASP), Certified Safety Professional (CSP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) certification.

The base salary range for this position is $127,000 to $157,000. These amounts reflect the range of base salary that the Institute reasonably would expect to pay a new hire or internal candidate for this position. The actual base compensation paid to any individual for this position may vary depending on factors such as experience, market conditions, education/training, skill level, and whether the compensation is internally equitable, and does not include bonuses, commissions, differential pay, other forms of compensation, or benefits. This position is also eligible to receive an annual discretionary bonus, with the amount dependent on individual and institute performance factors.

In addition to the Base Salary and Annual Bonus above, you will be eligible to participate in the Institute’s Compound Cash Grant Program (the “CCGP”). The CCGP is a program designed to offer multi-year cash grants providing for a fixed dollar amount paid out in semi-annual installments to reward employees for staying and contributing to the Institute. As soon as reasonably practical after your start date, you will receive a grant letter describing the terms of your award under the CCGP.

title: Technical Advisor, Subnational Data Use and Decision Science
description:
Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) is a global health organization that partners locally and globally to create and scale solutions to the world’s deadliest health threats. Millions of people die from preventable health threats. We collaborate to close the gap between proven, life-saving solutions and the people who need them. Since 2017, we’ve worked with governments and other partners in more than 60 countries to save millions of lives. We work toward a future where people live longer, healthier lives, communities flourish, and economies thrive. This is an ambitious vision, and it inspires us and our partners to make progress every day. 

Position Purpose

The Technical Advisor, Subnational Collaborative Surveillance Data Use and Decision Science, strengthens the integration, analysis, interpretation, and use of surveillance data in implementing states. As part of the Nigeria RTSL Collaborative Surveillance team, the Advisor supports state institutions and AFENET Nigeria in improving surveillance governance, collaboration, and sustainable epidemic intelligence functions. 

Initially supporting two selected States, the Advisor plans, coordinates, and delivers RTSL’s technical assistance across the surveillance data lifecycle, strengthening linkages among indicator- and event-based surveillance, laboratories, public health emergency operations centres, primary healthcare and other relevant sectors. The role supports states to strengthen the design, development, and routine use of priority information products—including weekly epidemiological reports, situation reports, 7-1-7 analyses, epidemiological bulletins and risk information products—as well as supporting routine use of  SITAware and 7-1-7 data to detect threats, monitor alerts, identify delays in detection, notification, investigation, confirmation and early response, analysing response timelines and informing public health decisions. 

Working with national and subnational technical teams, the Advisor strengthens the capacity of state teams through tailored training, hands-on mentorship and supportive supervision in data management, analysis, visualisation and interpretation, enabling them to produce high-quality information products independently and routinely translate analytical findings into timely, evidence-informed public health decisions and actions. 

The position reports directly to the Senior Technical Advisor, Health Security and Event-based Surveillance and collaborates closely with AFENET, state surveillance and emergency management teams, state primary healthcare institutions, state-based development partners, NCDC, RTSL Nigeria, and global teams. 

Work Location: This position is open to candidates based in Abuja, Nigeria

Duration: Full-time employment for a fixed term of 24 months with the possibility of renewal based on funding and mutual interest.

Core Responsibilities

The Technical Advisor will provide technical leadership, mentorship and quality assurance to strengthen subnational data use and decision science as part of Collaborative Surveillance. Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to, the following: 

Technical support and mentorship 

  • Provide technical leadership and guidance for the implementation of data use, epidemic-intelligence, and decision-science activities within subnational Collaborative Surveillance, , ensuring alignment with agreed program priorities, national standards, and state needs. 
  • Engage state directors, surveillance leaders, PHEOC managers and other decision-makers to identify and prioritise information needs for preparedness, detection, risk assessment, response and resource allocation. 
  • Develop and deliver structured capacity-strengthening activities in epidemiological analysis, R, data visualisation, interpretation, analytical communication and reproducible reporting. 
  • Provide hands-on mentorship and accompaniment to AFENET, state government and partner staff to strengthen their skills in data management, data pipeline development, and analysis, so they can routinely turn surveillance data into information that informs timely public health decisions. 

Epidemic intelligence and information products 

  • Lead or support co-design processes to prioritise and develop state-specific information products, including epidemiological bulletins, Situation Reports, epi risk bulletins, analytical briefs and leadership products. 
  • Provide technical oversight for data preparation, analysis, visualisation, interpretation and automation of priority information products. 
  • Promote reproducible analytical workflows and well-documented scripts using R that can be maintained and adapted by state and partner personnel. 
  • Establish and strengthen routine data-quality review, reconciliation and feedback processes and ensure that identified issues are tracked to resolution. 

SITAware, 7-1-7 and performance improvement 

  • In close collaboration with the Technical Advisor, Collaborative Surveillance and 717 Coordination, guide the systematic analysis of detection, notification, and response performance, and support state teams in identifying and resolving recurring bottlenecks. 
  • Provide hands-on mentorship and support to States on the use of SitAware, ensuring consistent documentation and updates of incidents and events on SitAware. 
  • Collaborate with the Data Engineer, Public Health Surveillance on future SITAware enhancements. 
  • Additional responsibilities may include gathering requirements for new SITAware features, directly conducting and coordinating user testing, SITAware user training, and ensuring that SITAware features align with subnational workflows. 

Representation, communication and reporting 

  • Represent RTSL in relevant technical working groups and subnational data-use forums, as delegated. 
  • Document implementation lessons, adaptations, effective practices and persistent constraints across participating states. 
  • Contribute to work plans, implementation reports, donor reports, learning briefs, case studies, presentations, and scalable implementation guidance. 
  • Provide regular technical updates on progress, risks, decisions, and follow-up actions to RTSL leadership and relevant counterparts. 
  • Perform other related duties consistent with the purpose of the position, as assigned by RTSL. 

Institutional Strengthening, Planning and Resource Optimisation 

  • Strengthen state institutional capacity to use surveillance, epidemic intelligence, and performance data for planning, prioritisation of resources, implementation, and routine tracking of health security interventions. 
  • Support states to integrate surveillance and performance priorities into implementation plans and trackers, linking identified gaps to activities, responsible teams, timelines, indicators, and expected results. 
  • Support routine analysis of implementation and performance data to identify gaps, bottlenecks and areas requiring corrective action, and ensure findings inform management and programme decisions. 
  • Support states to optimize and track available domestic and external financing, including the NCDC Gateway of the Basic Health Care Provision Fund (BHCPF) and World Bank-supported funding, by using an implementation tracker 
  • Build and sustain the capacity of state teams to independently maintain these planning, tracking and data-use processes as part of routine institutional systems. 

Qualifications

Education

  • Master’s degree in epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, public health, health informatics or a related field.  

Experience

  • Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible experience in public health data analytics, disease surveillance, epidemic intelligence, decision science or health informatics, preferably within or in close partnership with government public health institutions. 
  • Demonstrated experience leading the design, automation and routine use of surveillance information products and decision-support tools. 
  • Demonstrated experience applying statistical and epidemiological methods to public health preparedness and response questions. 
  • Demonstrated experience using statistical programming to conduct analyses and/or automate the generation of information products. 
  • Demonstrated experience in training, mentorship and capacity transfer for public health professionals and implementing partners. 

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong understanding of public health surveillance, epidemic intelligence, emergency management, and the role of data in preparedness, detection and response. 
  • Advanced proficiency in R for data preparation, descriptive and inferential analysis, visualisation, geospatial analysis and reproducible reporting. 
  • Excellent ability to translate complex analytical findings into concise, actionable messages for technical and non-technical decision makers. 
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation, negotiation and relationship-management skills across government, partner and donor audiences. 
  • Excellent technical writing, report writing, presentation, and verbal communication skills. 
  • Strong mentoring, coaching and team-development skills. 
  • Results- and impact-oriented, with sound judgment, a problem-solving approach and attention to detail. 
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across institutions and locations. 
  • Adaptability and cultural sensitivity, with the ability to tailor technical assistance to varying state capacities, operating environments and information needs. 
  • Ability and willingness to travel frequently within Nigeria, particularly to participating states and selected LGAs. This role is expected to involve 25% travel to the states.  
  • Fluency in written and spoken English is required. 

Preferred Qualifications:  

  • Strong understanding of the International Health Regulations (2005), Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response and One Health approaches  
  • Experience with SORMAS, SITAware, 7-1-7, laboratory information systems or public health emergency operations centres is desirable. 
  • A PhD in epidemiology, biostatistics, data science, public health, health informatics or a related field 

Compensation and Benefits

Resolve to Save Lives prides itself on cultivating a supportive, connected remote team doing work that matters. We do everything possible to ensure our employees are connected and set up for success. 

The salary for this role is competitive and set according to national labor rates for the NGO sector in Nigeria. The exact offer will be determined by various factors, such as the candidate’s skills and experience relative to the requirements of the role.   

In addition to a competitive salary, Resolve to Save Lives provides a generous package of benefits, including:

title: Literacy Coach
description:
About the Team

Michigan Online School (MOS) is a K-12 tuition-free online public school in the state of Michigan. At MOS, we empower students to be their best by enabling them to learn in ways that are right for them – using innovative technology at home, at their proper level, and at their own pace.

The Literacy Coach partners with teachers, school leaders, and instructional teams to strengthen literacy instruction and improve student achievement. Through job-embedded coaching, professional learning, collaborative planning, classroom modeling, and data-informed support, the Literacy Coach helps educators implement evidence-based literacy practices aligned with Michigan academic standards and state literacy initiatives.

The Literacy Coach works collaboratively with teachers, principals, leadership teams, and data specialists to build instructional capacity, support effective literacy interventions, strengthen reading outcomes, and promote continuous school improvement. This position emphasizes a collaborative, relationship-driven approach to professional growth and instructional excellence.

Eligibility: Open to residents of Michigan

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Instructional Coaching & Teacher Support

  • Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with teaching staff grounded in mutual respect, teamwork, and accountability.

  • Partner with classroom teachers to implement evidence-based early literacy instructional practices through job-embedded coaching.

  • Provide individualized and small-group coaching through classroom observations, instructional modeling, co-teaching, collaborative planning, goal-setting, and reflective conversations.

  • Model effective whole-group and small-group literacy instruction for teachers and students.

  • Support teachers in developing effective classroom literacy environments and implementing research-based instructional strategies and literacy programs.

  • Coach teachers in structured literacy lesson design and the implementation of practices aligned with state standards.

  • Provide ongoing feedback to help teachers reflect on, establish goals, practice, and refine instructional skills aligned with the Essential Instructional Practices in Literacy.

Data Analysis & Student Achievement

  • Analyze formative assessment, screening, and diagnostic data to develop and inform instructional plans.

  • Support teachers in collecting, analyzing, and using student data to guide instructional decisions and improve learning outcomes.

  • Administer and interpret universal screeners to identify students with characteristics of dyslexia.

  • Train and support teachers in identifying reading deficiencies and implementing appropriate evidence-based interventions.

  • Support the identification and implementation of instructional strategies to address students' individual literacy needs.

Professional Learning & School Leadership

  • Lead, organize, and facilitate professional learning communities (PLCs) and collaborative professional development opportunities for teachers.

  • Facilitate the school's literacy leadership committee and support the development of a comprehensive literacy continuum.

  • Assist building principals in identifying instructional strengths and areas of need related to literacy instruction.

  • Communicate student progress, instructional needs, and coaching outcomes with principals and school leadership teams.

  • Attend required coaching trainings, networking sessions, and professional learning opportunities.

  • Engage in continuous professional learning to remain current on research-supported literacy instruction, coaching practices, and the science of reading.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Valid Michigan teaching certificate.

  • Five or more years of successful teaching experience; virtual teaching experience preferred.

  • Experience facilitating professional learning at the grade-level or team level.

  • Demonstrated experience supporting students with dyslexia or characteristics of dyslexia, including the implementation of evidence-based reading interventions.

  • Training or certification in a dyslexia-focused instructional program.

  • Strong knowledge of reading and writing development, literacy acquisition, and evidence-based instructional practices.

  • Familiarity with Michigan's Dyslexia Handbook and state requirements related to early screening and intervention.

  • Knowledge of current Michigan literacy standards and legislation, including Public Acts 146 and 147.

  • Experience using formative assessments, universal screeners, and diagnostic assessment tools to inform instructional planning.

  • Ability to use classroom observation data and formative assessment practices to guide instructional coaching and professional learning.

  • Proficiency with technology-based instructional and organizational tools.

  • Demonstrated ability to build positive professional relationships and collaborate effectively with teachers, administrators, and other stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Literacy or a related field, or Reading Specialist certification.

  • LETRS training or equivalent professional learning focused on research-based early literacy practices and the science of reading.

  • Additional training or certification in evidence-based structured literacy instruction.

About Us

“We believe that every child should be able to be anything they want in life, regardless of their birthplace and circumstances.” – Ron Packard, CEO & Founder

ACCEL Schools is a network of 80+ high-performing, public charter schools serving PK-12 students. We proudly advocate for school choice and work to address educational inequities throughout the United States. Our schools are inclusive and widely differ to reflect the unique values of the many urban, suburban, and rural communities we serve.
